source.title: Path Regularization: A Convexity and Sparsity Inducing Regularization for Parallel ReLU Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-based training outcomes on a toy dataset and UCI classification datasets, extending the training-success question to settings outside the claim versions’ named benchmarks and architectures.
record.gate_note: CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST results are test-accuracy plots, not training-error results. The paper cites prior work on local minima and overparameterization; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports related optimization results, but tests none of V1–V6. Its toy experiment varies the number of three-layer parallel subnetworks and measures a regularized objective; it does not test V2's two-layer teacher-student width intervention. Its unit training accuracy results concern fully connected UCI classifiers rather than V1's convolutional CIFAR networks. The remaining experiments do not measure the interventions and training outcomes named in V3–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive an exact convex formulation for the three-layer path-regularized parallel ReLU problem, subject to sufficient subnetworks, and a low-rank approximation with global objective guarantees. They interpret the toy experiment as showing that additional subnetworks improve SGD convergence toward the convex optimum. Table 2 shows approximation to, rather than numerical equality with, the reported 0.0007 optimum even at K=40.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies path-regularized parallel ReLU networks and compares non-convex SGD/Adam with a proposed convex formulation; the claim versions focus on other interventions and conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of parallel subnetworks K changes how often toy SGD trials reach the convex method’s global minimum; CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST test-accuracy curves differ in reported performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five SGD initializations per condition, toy regularized objectives range from 0.0027–0.0239 at K=5, 0.0009–0.0027 at K=20, and 0.0008–0.0009 at K=40, against a convex reference of 0.0007. The authors interpret this as improved convergence with more subnetworks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the number of parallel subnetworks can improve SGD's attained regularized training objective in a three-layer ReLU toy problem.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that all compared algorithms were trained until unit training accuracy on the selected 21 UCI datasets; dataset-specific training accuracies and training durations are not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested parallel fully connected classifiers can attain unit training accuracy on these small UCI binary classification datasets.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023, as stated in the text)
record.problems: The toy comparison uses five initialization trials per K and reports training objectives rather than classification error. The UCI training-accuracy statement is aggregate and does not provide dataset-specific values. CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST results shown are test accuracy, not training error.
record.rows_left_out: None. CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST test-accuracy results were left out because they do not measure the training-error behavior in the claim.

untested.parts: Training classification error for sufficiently large convolutional CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 networks, corrupted or random labels, and the specified smaller-model or regularization qualifications.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems as teacher and student grow together, and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy gain, learning-rate tolerance and stability, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: A new dataset alone does not justify T3 when the architecture, intervention or measure fails to match every supplied version. Neither finite-run suboptimal objectives nor the authors' convergence interpretation independently establish that those runs ended in spurious local minima.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, or results with corrupted or random labels.
The study does not test the two-layer teacher-student setting or compare student width with teacher width.
No depth comparison tests plain networks against identity shortcuts for training error.
No initialization comparison tests training speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability or sharpness experiment is reported.
No batch-normalization comparison measures training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
